turns.content: Write both sorted 100-card hands as A: A={a_1<...<a_100} and A={b_1<...<b_100}. Using only their relative order, construct a valid family based on a single order statistic and show that its members are distinct.

Generalize to n cards per hand and introduce an order symbol for the winner relation. For each j, form the two complementary canonical hands {1,...,j} union {n+j+1,...,2n} and {j+1,...,n+j}; identify the first decisive index for an arbitrary valid rule.
For disjoint X={x_1<...<x_n} and X={y_1<...<y_n}, assume x_k<y_k. Construct fresh n-sets U, V, and W whose interleaving realizes the canonical comparisons at k-1 and k.
Which comparisons between the original hands and the auxiliary sets follow immediately from coordinatewise dominance?
Use relative-order invariance and transitivity to assemble the comparison chain relevant to the proposed classification, including its endpoint case.
What does that chain establish about the winner and the proposed classification?
Explain whether this classification exhausts the valid rules and identify the invariance property used in the argument.
Apply the resulting classification to 100-card hands and determine the number of valid rules.
